transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... I guess I'm here because of these small spaces. Like, if I get into a slow elevator or... or a small room where the door locks. My chest just jumps right away. I don't know, I just get this really strong need to get out... before I can even think straight.
Do these feelings of panic only happen in specific situations, like small spaces, or do they sometimes come up unexpectedly even when you're not in those situations?

No, it's just... just in those spots. I know a little storage room or... an elevator at the museum, I know it ain't the same as being locked up. But my mind just treats it like trouble. Soon as I see there's no window and the door shuts tight... that's when it happens. Not really out of nowhere.
Do you find yourself actively avoiding places or situations where you might experience these feelings, like avoiding elevators or small rooms altogether?

Yeah, I suppose I do. I... I just take the stairs mostly. Or, you know, at the museum where I volunteer, I just pass on any jobs down in the archives. If I absolutely have to go into a tight spot, I... well, I might ask someone to just wait outside the door for me. It's a bit foolish at my age, but... yeah, I avoid them.
When you're in these small spaces and start feeling panicky, does it build up very quickly—like within a few minutes—and feel like a sudden wave of intense fear?
I... I don't really know about a wave. I couldn't say if it's a few minutes or what. I just... I just know I need to get out of there. I don't pay much mind to the rest of it.
When you're in a small space and you start feeling panicky, does the feeling come on suddenly and reach its peak within just a few minutes?

Well... like I just said, I couldn't rightly tell you. I don't time it or nothing. I just... I just feel it and know I need to get out. I don't know about any peaks. That's really all I can tell you about it.
When you start feeling panicky in a small space, does it come on suddenly and reach its worst point within just a few minutes?
Look, Doc... I thought I just answered this. I don't know how fast it happens. I'm not looking at my watch. I just get uncomfortable and want to leave. That's... that's all there is to it.
When you enter a small space, does the panic or uncomfortable feeling start right away, as soon as you're inside, or does it come on more gradually?

Well... yeah, I suppose it's right away. Soon as I step into one of them slow elevators or... or a small room where the door's shut tight. My chest just jumps. Before I can even think straight, I just... I just know I need to get back out. That's about it.
When you start feeling panicky in a small space, does the feeling get really intense very quickly, like within just a few minutes?

Doc, I... I feel like we're going in circles here. I really don't know what else to tell you. Like I just said, it happens right away. I ain't counting the minutes to see how intense it gets... I just know I gotta get out. That's all I got for you.
Have you ever experienced sudden panic or fear that came out of the blue, without being triggered by a small space or similar situation?
No... no, it's just the small spaces. That's it. Never had it happen out of nowhere.
When you start feeling panicky in a small space, does the fear or discomfort get really intense very quickly, like within a few minutes?
Didn't we... didn't we just go over this? Like I said before, I don't know anything about how many minutes it takes. It just happens, and I gotta get out. I don't keep track of the time.
When you start feeling panicky in a small space, does the discomfort or fear reach its worst point very quickly, like within just a few minutes?
Look... I just... I don't know what else to say. You keep asking the same thing. I don't time it. It just gets bad and I leave. That's all I know.
When you start feeling panicky in a small space, does the fear or discomfort reach its worst point within just a few minutes?
Doc... I don't understand why you keep asking me the exact same thing. I already told you, I don't know. I don't have a watch out when it happens. It just gets bad, and that's all I can tell you.
When the fear or discomfort starts in a small space, does it get as bad as it’s going to get very quickly, like within just a few minutes?
I... I really don't know what you want me to say anymore. I ain't got a different answer for you. I just don't know.
When you go into a small space, does the fear always happen the same way each time, or does it sometimes catch you by surprise even when you're in a similar situation?
I... I guess it's mostly the same. If I go in, I get scared. That's about it.
When you start feeling panicky in a small space, do you also notice other physical symptoms like sweating, shaking, or having trouble breathing?
I ain't really noticed all that. I just... I get scared, like I said. I don't think I'm shaking or sweating or nothing. I just want out of there.
Do you ever feel panicky or uncomfortable in other kinds of enclosed or crowded places, like movie theaters, public transportation, or even standing in a long line outside?
No, I don't think so. It's just... just the small places. I don't really go to the movies or ride the bus anyway.
When you start feeling panicky in a small space, does the fear or discomfort go away quickly once you leave the situation, like within a few minutes?
Yeah, I suppose. Once I'm out, I'm alright. It doesn't last long after I get away from it.
